supporting_observations.claim: At 13:40:33 UTC, WS-MSANTOS-01's computer account obtained Kerberos tickets from DC-BLU-01; at 13:40:35, LDAP traffic and a network logon by WS-MSANTOS-01$ were recorded. These records identify authentication and directory traffic, not a PowerShell process or its operator.
The supplied records contain no process-creation event, PowerShell command line, or other direct evidence confirming what caused the reported window around 13:40 UTC.

At 13:43 UTC, WS-MSANTOS-01 used the Windows Update Agent to connect to download.windowsupdate.com; the proxy record reports about 38.8 MB received. This is consistent with update activity, but does not establish that it caused the reported PowerShell window.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied evidence has no process-creation or PowerShell-specific telemetry for the reported time; the nearby records show network and authentication activity only (T194-00146 through T194-00156).
The available records do not show the screen, interactive session, script contents, or user action associated with the reported window.
claims_not_established: Whether a PowerShell process actually ran on WS-MSANTOS-01 around 13:40 UTC, and if so, its command line, parent process, integrity level, and outcome.
Whether the activity was initiated by Mia, IT, another user, or an automated task.
Whether the nearby authentication and directory traffic or the later Windows Update transfer was related to the reported window.
additional_evidence_needed: Retrieve endpoint process and PowerShell telemetry for WS-MSANTOS-01 around 13:35–13:45 UTC, including Sysmon/Windows process-creation events, PowerShell operational logs, EDR process trees, and command-line data.

Check task scheduler, software-update, and management-tool logs for activity on WS-MSANTOS-01 around 13:40 UTC, and confirm with Mia whether the window coincided with an expected update or other action.
If process evidence is found, collect the relevant script or file, hash, signature, and execution outcome.
unrelated_findings: At 13:42–13:43 UTC, authentication for ruth.moss originated from WS-MSANTOS-01 and was followed by network logons on WS-RMOSS-01; a certificate-based Kerberos pre-authentication event for ruth.moss was also recorded. This is separate from the reported 13:40 PowerShell activity and merits review in a separate ticket (T194-00161, T194-00165, T194-00172, T194-00175).

At 14:15–14:16 UTC, Mia's workstation accessed Slack and Google Drive, services not listed as approved in the supplied environment context. These records show web access, not file upload or transfer, and should be reviewed separately (T194-00289, T194-00290, T194-00327, T194-00328).
